item.title: Future Hogs – Week 3: College football players who could help the Commanders
item.description: Scouting college prospects for the Washington Commanders
item.content:encoded:
It did not look like the premier matchup of Week 3 of the college football between LSU and Ole Miss would live up to the hype. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss looked like a Heisman front-runner in the first half, converting all his third downs and leading the Rebels to a 24-7 lead at the half. Lane Kiffin motivated the Tigers at halftime as they rallied to tie the game at 24-24 in the fourth quarter. Chambliss had a little magic left as he led the Rebels to the go ahead touchdown and two-point conversion. A tipped pass in the end zone on LSU’s final drive resulted in an interception of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt that sealed the win for Ole Miss.

The other ranked-on-ranked games were competitive games. Louisville and SMU was a back and forth affair with Louisville taking the lead in the fourth quarter and holding on to it for the win. A failed two-point conversion allowed Texas Tech to escape an upset by Houston. Who didn’t escape being upset this weekend? Texas A&M. Despite being tied with Kentucky at halftime, 21 unanswered points in the third quarter was enough for a Wildcats win. Virginia will fall from the AP Top 25 after a loss to West Virginia.

Week 4 will feature a pivotal matchup between #10 LSU and #23 Texas A&M. A second loss for either team could end their chances for the College Football Playoff. #1 Texas will go on the road to #14 Tennessee in each team’s first SEC action. Several Big Ten teams will begin conference play. This includes #18 Michigan as they welcome #17 Iowa, a team that may finally have some offensive firepower, and #20 Oregon who will go on the road to face #12 USC who are looking to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to comment with players that stood out to you.

Aidan Chiles | QB | Senior | Northwestern

It was tough to see Jayden Daniels injure his elbow for a third time in the past year. While he has the talent of a top NFL QB, his health has to be a consideration with regards to his future in Washington. While I’m not at the point where the team should consider an early draft pick to replace him, it shows why it’s always important to continually look for talent at the position.

Aidan Chiles has played at Oregon State, Michigan State, and now Northwestern. He’s had an up and down career. He was benched last season at Michigan State as he and the team struggled. He decided to transfer to Northwestern and, so far, it looks like a good decision. Chiles is 6’4”, 225 pounds, so plenty of size for the position. When Chiles has times, he has good mechanics and delivers accurate passes. When he has to get rid of the ball quickly, those mechanics change and his accuracy can dip. While Chiles can run, he is more of a pocket passer with a strong enough arm for NFL throws. Chiles went 17 of 22 for 241 yards and three touchdowns and two touchdowns on the ground.

Keyjuan Brown | RB | Senior | Louisville

David Blough might have felt pressure to pass with how effectively Dallas scored, but there were moments in the run game. Although more attention has been given to his teammate and backfield-mate Isaac Brown, Keyjuan Brown looks more like a complete NFL back. He’s densely built at 5’10”, 215 pounds, but he has superb burst and speed at that size. Those qualities along with his vision make him a productive back in a zone blocking scheme. While he can lower his shoulder and deliver punishment, he’d much rather use his quick feet to juke tacklers. Where he isn’t much of a contributor is in the pass game since he only has 18 receptions in his career. Louisville got the win over SMU behind Keyjuan Brown’s 163 yards and two touchdown on 10 attempts.

Junior Sherrill | WR | Senior | Vanderbilt

The receivers for the Commanders were a mixed bag against Dallas. While Stefon Diggs had a respectable game, Terry McLaurin struggled. Dyami Brown made a few plays, but had a costly fumble. Antonio Williams made three catches, but wasn’t as impactful as he was in Week 1. Junior Sherrill fits the mold of receivers like Williams and Diggs. His route-running creates separation against defenders thanks to his nuance and attention to detail. His hands are reliable both as a receiver and a kick returner. After the catch, he has both elusiveness and toughness thanks to his 5’11”, 200 pound frame. My biggest question about his game is deep speed; he’ll make deep catches, but just doesn’t look like a burner. Sherrill had six catches, 108 yards, and two touchdowns in Vanderbilt’s win over NC State.

Luke Reynolds | TE | Junior | Virginia Tech

With Chig Okonkwo hurt for the matchup with Dallas, the tight ends were not factors in the pass game. Luke Reynolds could change that. He followed James Franklin to Blacksburg from Penn State and he has shined in an increased role this season. It is hard to believe a tight end this athletic and quick is 6’4”, 250 pounds. Quickness and agility allows him to create separation when running routes and eluding tacklers after the catch. Reynolds adjusts easily to passes thanks to above-average body control. The blocking needs work. He will try to block, but his technique needs improvement in order for him to sustain blocks. Reynolds made 12 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Hokies win over Maryland.

Kade Pieper | OG | RS Junior | Iowa

It looked like the interior offensive line struggled opening holes in the run game early, but improved as the game went on. Pass protection was better than last week, but there is still need for improvement. Enter Kade Pieper. Now 6’3”, 293 pounds is small for an offensive lineman, but he is an athlete. He’s got elite quickness, an attribute necessary to play center. It also helps him in the zone blocking game reaching his landmarks. While he might be a smaller offensive line, Piper is strong. He anchors well against power and drives his legs to get movement as a run blocker. Iowa put up 55 points and over 600 yards against Northern Iowa behind Pieper and the offensive line.

Will Echoles | DL | Junior | Ole Miss

The Commanders’ run defense was a bright spot, but they need to add more to the defensive line. Daron Payne is in a contract year and Johnny Newton, who is recovering from a pectoral injury, has not impressed.

A lot of attention is given to Trinidad Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense, but Will Echoles may be the Rebels best draft prospect. Echoles has the size to play anywhere on a defensive interior at 6’3”, 315 pounds. What stands out right away is Echoles’ quickness. His hands are lightning fast and he slips by defenders so easily. This makes him so disruptive even if he doesn’t finish the play. He plays low and keeps leverage against blockers, controlling them until he can dispose of them when he gets to the ball. As a true junior, Echoles should only get stronger and more impactful. Echoles finished the day with five tackles, 2.5 for a loss, and half a sack in Ole Miss’ victory against LSU.

Owen Long | LB | Junior | Arizona State

Frankie Luvu was missed in Dallas. Leo Chenal looked unaware of his coverage assignments. Owen Long is only a junior, but he was all over the field for the Sun Devils as they took down Kansas. A transfer from Colorado State, Long led college football in total tackles last season. He’s smaller at 6’1”, 225 pounds, but it helps with his ability to move around the field. That makes him an asset in coverage and helps him make tackles out to the sidelines. He will have to put on some size to take on blockers in the run game, but he could be a good depth player that gives the Commanders some versatility in the middle of the defense. Long’s contribution to the Arizona State win: 12 tackles, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and an interception.

Chris Peal | CB | Senior | Syracuse

Against Dallas, any cornerback not named Amik Robertson struggled. While Mike Sainristil had a better game, he was still targeted often by Dak Prescott. Rasul Douglas did not do much better. Maybe Chris Peal can help with that. He’s got great size at 6’1”, 200 pounds, and he has long arms that help him break up passes. He moves fluidly which helps him mirror receivers throughout their routes. He is active in run support and rarely misses tackles. The big knock against him is he has no interceptions in his career. In a loss to Pitt, Peal had three tackles and a PBU.

Kingston Lopa | S | RS Sophomore | California

The Commanders need to improve their coverage in the middle of the field. While Jeremy Reaves is a fan favorite for good reason, he’s a tick slow to recognize the developing play or just a little too slow to make a play. Given he’s only a redshirt sophomore, Kingston Lopa may not declare for the draft this year. His stock, however, may not be higher. He has five interceptions on the season playing in the middle of the Golden Bears secondary. He’s a tall safety at 6’5”, 210 pounds. You’d think it’d make it hard for him to change direction, but he flips his hips smoothly in coverage. He’s comfortable in both man and zone coverages with no problem making a play on the ball. One place where he could improve is his physicality around the line of scrimmage. Cal has been putting defensive backs into the league and Lopa looks to be next in line. He had five tackles, one for a loss, and an interception in a win over Wagner.

Which college players caught your eye in Week 3 and could help the Washington Commanders?

item.title: Chargers Daily Links: Bolts select Oklahoma DT in updated 2027 NFL mock draft
item.description: The Chargers are paired with Oklahoma DT David Stone in a new updated 2027 NFL mock draft.
item.content:encoded:
Good morning, Chargers fans!

At 0-2, the trajectory of the Bolts this season is firmly downward. A look at the league’s No. 1 most difficult schedule from Week Three on could very well turn in to a top-five pick in next year’s draft if things don’t take a drastic turn.

However, this new updated 2027 mock draft from Yahoo Sports still has the Chargers picking at No. 17, meaning they believe the Bolts will settle in and finish with around 8-9 wins this year. That sounds like a miracle at the current moment, but something the fan base will surely take if they could have it.

At pick No. 17, analyst Curt Popejoy has the Chargers selecting Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone. Stone stands 6’3 and looks incredibly-lean for someone listed at 315 pounds. He has the mass to play anywhere along the interior of the line all while also offering the upside of a pass rush with his excellent get-off and notable length.

Defensive tackle likely isn’t the position the Chargers will need to address the most come next year’s draft, but picking a blue-chip player at an impact position in today’s NFL is always a strong backup option if there is not an elite offensive lineman or skill player available when they’re on the clock.

item.title: Fantasy football waiver wire: 14 players to add for NFL Week 3
item.description: If you lost your starting QB to injury, here are some potential replacements. In addition, these draft-day afterthoughts may have staying power.
item.content:encoded:
It was quite a weekend of quarterback carnage in the NFL.

Week 2 gave us injuries to Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Jaxson Dart to add to the early-season collection. And now fantasy managers are the ones scrambling − to find a starter for this week's matchup.

(It's yet another example of why you should always get a backup quarterback on draft day. Unless you have an extremely small bench, the position is just too valuable to rely on finding a free agent QB the moment you need one.)

The waiver wire this week may or may not help fantasy managers who lost their starting quarterback to injury. If there's a silver lining, it's that Kyler Murray and Michael Penix Jr. are now healthy enough to reclaim the starting jobs in Minnesota and Atlanta. But having more choices may just make the problem worse.

Fantasy football quarterbacks to add for Week 3

Due to the wide variance in types of leagues and individual team needs, the players listed here include their availability rates in Yahoo leagues, which may or may not match rates on other platforms. (Suggested bid values based on $100 free agent acquisition budget for the season.)

For customized waiver wire suggestions, synced to your league, subscribe to USA TODAY Sports Fantasy's exclusive tools.

QB Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers (33% rostered)

No need to panic. Young is the QB2 after the first two weeks and is available in two out of every three leagues. But the other managers in your league who lost their quarterback will have him at the top of their list, too. How confident are we in this being a true breakout season for him? Coach Dave Canales, now in his third season with Carolina, is one of the better offensive minds in the league. Young has some decent weapons around him. We're buying in ... but it may be costly. (Recommended FAAB bid: $18. More if you lost Daniels)

QB Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints (48%)

Shough is the QB6 so far, and Chris Olave is an elite receiver. That makes him an attractive pickup if you miss out on Young. His rushing ability is a bonus. (FAAB bid: $10)

QB C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans (39%)

Stroud threw for 353 yards against what looks like a pretty good Bengals defense. And that was without star receiver Nico Collins on the field. The Texans didn't find the end zone all day, but getting Collins back should help considerably. (FAAB bid: $8)

QB Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (5%)

Cousins has thrown for three touchdowns in each of his first two games as a Raider. How much do we believe in his impressive start? Considering he hasn't had star TE Brock Bowers so far − and Bowers is poised to return from his knee cleanup procedure this week − there may be even better days ahead. Consider Cousins a short-term pickup for now with top draft pick Fernando Mendoza still waiting in the wings. (FAAB bid: $4)

More fantasy football players to add for Week 3

RB Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (27%)

With J.K. Dobbins exiting early with an injury and RJ Harvey inactive, Coleman got a chance to shine. The numbers weren't spectacular (10 carries, 39 yards) but he did get into the end zone in the fourth quarter. If you didn't lose a quarterback, Coleman should be the top waiver-wire priority this week for his significant upside. (FAAB bid: $18)

WR Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns (32%)

The Browns are going to have to throw the ball a lot this season. QB Deshaun Watson almost looked competent doing it in a Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Boston caught five passes for 95 yards on Sunday, and he has a long TD reception in each of the Browns' first two games. This may be your last chance to buy in. (FAAB bid: $11)

TE Dalton Schultz, Houston Texans (57%)

If you're getting frustrated by Colston Loveland's struggles or lost Dallas Goedert to injury, Schultz could be the right man at the right time. His 12 receptions for 140 yards in Week 2 were a product of Nico Collins missing the game, but the rapport he has with Stroud should keep him heavily involved in the passing game all season long. (FAAB bid: $8)

WR Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders (29%)

Tucker led the Raiders in Week 2 with 119 receiving yards, 40 of them coming on a second-quarter TD. Bowers' return will eat into his target share, but as long as Cousins has time to throw there should be enough opportunities for everyone. (FAAB bid: $7)

RB Emmanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks (1%)

The former Packer was thrust into a larger role than expected when rookie Jadarian Price had to leave with a chest injury. Wilson carried the ball 21 times for 92 yards, further enhancing his value as a capable backup. He could be a sneaky-good start against the Commanders in Week 3 if Price is limited. (FAAB bid: $7)

WR Devaughn Vele, New Orleans Saints (51%)

We all know about Chris Olave, but the third-year pro seems to be de-Vele-ping into a nice complementary receiver on the other side. He didn't find the end zone in Week 2, but Vele caught five of his seven targets for 64 yards. His consistency has been impressive as he's stepped into the role we expected for rookie Jordyn Tyson before he was injured. (FAAB bid: $6)

WR Romeo Doubs, New England Patriots (15%)

The Patriots haven't been as potent on offense as they were last season. The loss of star wideout A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain hasn't helped. Doubs was on the receiving end of a 63-yard bomb that was one of the few big plays in a 20-3 slog over the Steelers. If QB Drake Maye is going to get back to last season's MVP-caliber form, Doubs will have to play a bigger role. (FAAB bid: $5)

WR Kalif Raymond, Chicago Bears (9%)

The uncertainty surrounding Caleb Williams is undertandable, but despite a 9-3 loss in Week 2, the Bears are still averaging over 30 points per game! Surprisingly, Raymond − not Loveland or Luther Burden or Rome Odunze − leads the team in targets (14), catches (13) and receiving yards (124) after two weeks. He should remain an important part of the passing game no matter who's behind center. (FAAB bid: $4)

RB Tank Bigsby, Philadelphia Eagles (29%)

Starter Saquon Barkley left early with a neck stinger against the Titans, leaving Bigsby and Jordan Shipley to fill the void. Shipley was on the field for more snaps, and Barkley eventually returned, but Bigsby got the ball at the goal line and punched it in from two yards out. He'll have more value if Barkley is limited going forward. (FAAB bid: $3)

TE Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (3%)

Are we doing this again? Remember last season when Waller caught a pair of TD passes in his Dolphins debut, then had scores in back-to-back games before becoming mostly invisible the rest of the way? It could be more of the same for the now 34-year-old. Waller's three-catch, two-touchdown outing in Week 2 shows he can be an effective red-zone target, But it's gong to be hard to count on him to score every week. (FAAB bid: $2)

item.title: Patriots vs. Steelers snap counts: Kyle Williams’ role remains unchanged
item.description: Notes and thoughts on the Patriots’ snap counts from their 20-3 win over the Steelers.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots entered their Week 2 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers with the task of replacing A.J. Brown, who had suffered a high-ankle sprain in the season opener. Among the candidates to fill Brown’s spot as a starting outside receiver was second-year man Kyle Williams, the speedster who looked good in preseason and entered the year poised for a bigger role.

He keeps waiting for it, however. Versus Pittsburgh, after all, Williams’ role remained unchanged: he served as a rotational package player on offense, taking the. field for just 11 of 55 offensive snaps — a similar share than last week versus the Seahawks.

Williams did manage to reel in a 10-yard pass on a 3rd-and-6 in the third quarter for his first catch of the season, but other than that and an incomplete target in the fourth period was quiet. To replace Brown, the Patriots instead relied on a three-receiver package of Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins. It was the same grouping they used down the stretch in Week 1.

Even though the season is still long and Brown reportedly expected to miss five more games after this one, it seems Williams’ position on the depth chart is set in stone for now.

Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 20-3 win at Gillette Stadium.

Offense

Total snaps: 55 | Time on the field: 26:16 | *denotes starter

QB Drake Maye* (55; 100%), LT Will Campbell* (55; 100%), LG Alijah Vera-Tucker* (55; 100%), C Jared Wilson* (55; 100%), RT Morgan Moses* (51; 93%), TE Hunter Henry* (50; 91%), RG Greg Van Roten (40; 73%), WR Mack Hollins (39; 71%), WR Romeo Doubs* (37; 67%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (33; 60%), WR DeMario Douglas* (26; 47%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (20; 36%), FB Reggie Gilliam (20; 36%), RG Mike Onwenu* (15; 27%), TE Cameron Latu (14; 25%), WR Kyle Williams (11; 20%), TE Eli Raridon* (11; 20%), WR Efton Chism III (10; 18%), RB Corey Kiner (4; 7%), RT Caleb Lomu (4; 7%)

Injuries were one of the biggest stories of the game, and the Patriots offense suffered two of them. The most significant was starting right guard Mike Onwenu, who exited the game in the late first quarter due to what was later reported as a broken ankle. With him out, veteran Greg Van Roten — who arrived in training camp — was moved into the top lineup between center Jared Wilson and right tackle Morgan Moses.

The other injury was suffered by rookie tight end Eli Raridon, who suffered a tight injury in the first half and was later ruled out for the remainder of the game. This means increased opportunities for Cameron Latu, another late addition to the roster. Latu played his first 14 snaps on offense against the Steelers, primarily serving as an in-line run blocker.

Speaking of firsts, Caleb Lomu also played his first offensive snaps. The first-round draft pick replaced the aforementioned Morgan Moses for the final four snaps of the game. As opposed to Onwenu and Raridon, Moses was not removed from the game due to injury.

Elsewhere on offense, TreVeyon Henderson out-snapped Rhamondre Stevenson following the latter’s first-quarter fumble. Efton Chism, meanwhile, played his first 10 snaps of the year after being a healthy scratch in Week 1; another byproduct of the A.J. Brown injury.

Defense

Total snaps: 70 | Time on the field: 30:51 | *denotes starter

LB Robert Spillane* (7o; 100%), LB Christian Elliss* (7o; 100%), CB Christian Gonzalez* (7o; 100%), S Kevin Byard III* (7o; 100%), CB Marcus Jones* (69; 99%), CB Charles Woods (60; 86%), ED Elijah Ponder* (54; 77%), ED Gabe Jacas (49; 70%), S Craig Woodson* (46; 66%), DT Milton Williams* (44; 63%), DT Christian Barmore* (36; 51%), DT Cory Durden* (34; 49%), S Jaylen Reed (28; 40%), DT Joshua Farmer (24; 34%), ED Dre’Mont Jones* (18; 26%), ED Quintayvious Hutchins (16; 23%), DT DaQuan Jones (10; 14%), CB Channing Canada (2; 3%)

New England’s safety depth was tested against the Steelers. Under normal circumstances, Craig Woodson would have played more than his 46 snaps, but the shoulder injury he suffered in the third quarter forced him to exit the contest. The nominal next man up, Dell Pettus, had already exited the game at that point: Pettus suffered an ankle ailment in the second period. This meant that Jaylen Reed saw his first defensive snaps since arriving in Foxborough via trade in late August.

The team also had to rely on its youth on the edge. With Dre’Mont Jones being lost for the game in the second quarter, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas ended up playing 54 and 49 snaps, respectively. In the meantime, Qunitayvious Hutchins also saw his first career reps on defense.

The same was true for Channing Canada, who briefly replaced fellow cornerback Marcus Jones in the late second quarter. Outside of his brief injury scare, however, Jones was on the field for every snap; with Carlton Davis inactive due to injury, the Patriots made the veteran slot their No. 2 cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez. In base sets, he lined up outside while kicking in in nickel and dime looks while Charles Woods was brought onto the field.

Elsewhere, recently-signed DaQuan Jones played 10 snaps in his Patriots debut.

Special teams

Total snaps: 25 | Time on the field: 2:53

TE Cameron Latu (21; 84%), LB Namdi Obiazor (20; 80%), S Jaylen Reed (18; 72%), LB Darius Muasau (16; 64%), CB Channing Canada (16; 64%), FB Reggie Gilliam (14; 56%), CB Karon Prunty (13; 52%), ED Gabe Jacas (12; 48%), LB Erick Hunter (12; 48%), CB Charles Woods (11; 44%), K Andy Borregales (10; 40%), DT Cory Durden (9; 36%), ED Elijah Ponder (9; 36%), ED Quintayvious Hutchins (9; 36%), LS Julian Ashby (9; 36%), P/H Mitch Wishnowsky (9; 36%), WR Efton Chism III (8; 32%), CB/PR Marcus Jones (8; 32%), S Dell Pettus (8; 32%), OT Will Campbell (5; 20%), OT Caleb Lomu (5; 20%), OL Alijah Vera-Tucker (5; 20%), OL Greg Van Roten (5; 20%), OL Ben Brown (5; 20%), S Craig Woodson (5; 20%), DT Milton Williams (4; 16%), DT Christian Barmore (4; 16%), LB Robert Spillane (2; 8%), WR/KR Kyle Williams (1; 4%), WR Mack Hollins (1; 4%), OL Mike Onwenu (1; 4%)

The Patriots used five players on their core-four special teams units, with Cameron Latu, Namdi Obiazor, Jaylen Reed, Darius Muasau and Gabe Jacas the only ones playing on kickoff return, kickoff coverage, punt return, and punt coverage. Latu, Obiazor, Muasau and Jacas all registered tackles among them, with the latter adding his special teams performance to an already strong defensive showing.

New England’s injuries also impacted the kicking game personnel. One position stands out in that regard: Dell Pettus (1), Craig Woodson (2) and Jaylen Reed (1) all saw snaps as the personal punt protector.

Did not play

QB Tommy DeVito

While the Steelers decided to insert their backup quarterback, Mason Rudolph, in the late fourth quarter, the Patriots did not use their QB2 on Sunday. For a second straight game, Tommy DeVito remained on the bench throughout the contest.

Inactive

QB3 Behren Morton, TE Tanner Arkin, OT Dametrious Crownover, OL Walter Rouse, DT Leonard Taylor III, CB Carlton Davis III

With only one practice squad elevation — punter Mitch Wishnowsky — the Patriots declared just six players as inactive for Sunday’s game. Two of those were ruled out because of injury: Dametrious Crownover and Carlton Davis were unavailable for the contest due to their respective knee and neck injuries. The other four were all healthy scratches, including Tanner Arkin and Leonard Taylor; both were on the game day roster in Week 1 but demoted against the Steelers.

item.title: Ranking NFL’s 0-2 teams by chances to actually make the playoffs
item.description: Which 0-2 NFL teams should still be thinking about the playoffs?
item.content:encoded:
After two weeks of NFL action, only eight teams are still without a win.

But with the league’s expansion to a 17-game schedule, as well as the expanded playoff format, an 0-2 start is no longer the deathblow for a team’s playoff chances. Last year alone the Houston Texans, the Chicago Bears, and the Carolina Panthers all made the playoffs despite dropping their first two games.

Which 0-2 teams could follow suit this year?

Here are those eight 0-2 teams, ranked by their playoff chances.

8. Atlanta Falcons

Where do we even begin?

The Falcons at least kept matters close in Week 1, losing to the Pittsburgh Steelers by a final score of 20-13. The decisive play, however, speaks to arguably their biggest problem as Cooper Rush threw a tough Pick-Six early in the fourth quarter to gift Pittsburgh a 20-10 lead.

Last Sunday against the Carolina Panthers was another story, as the Falcons never looked in the game from the start — when Rush lost a fumble on the first play from scrimmage — and a 34-3 loss was what waited for them.

Michael Penix Jr. will be back for Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers, which could give the offense a boost. But this is a team that looks a long way from a playoff spot.

Yet, you will see a lot of them, as right now Atlanta’s next three games are prime-time affairs. Rejoice!

7. Miami Dolphins

Two trips west, and two losses for the Miami Dolphins to start the season.

Last Sunday’s 35-13 loss to the San Francisco 49ers might be expected, but it is the opening-week loss to the Las Vegas Raiders that is more worrisome. Miami has struggled on both sides of the football through two weeks, and ranks near the bottom of the league in several categories, including scoring offense (30th), total offense (27th), and scoring defense (30th).

When might the wins come?

The Dolphins get to play at home for two of their next three games, which is the good news. The bad news? Those are games against the Chiefs and the Bengals, a pair of 2-0 teams, and those games sandwich a trip to Minnesota to take on the 2-0 Vikings.

Miami is in a rebuild, so an 0-2 start is not entirely unexpected.

Turning this around for a playoff push, however, would be unexpected.

6. Washington Commanders

It was tough to watch Jayden Daniels dislocate his left elbow again in Sunday’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Dan Quinn said the team will rally around backup Marcus Mariota, and the veteran does give Washington a fighting chance each week. But with games coming up against Seattle, Indianapolis, the Giants, San Francisco, Philadelphia, and the Rams, Daniels going down comes ahead of a rather tough stretch of games.

Maybe Washington steals a game or two, but even that would mean overcoming a 2-6 start which seems like too high of a hill to climb.

5. Tennessee Titans

On the positive side of the ledger, the Tennessee Titans were two minutes away from knocking off the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

On the negative side of the ledger, that was enough time for Jalen Hurts to engineer a game-winning drive, as he connected with Darius Cooper on a short touchdown pass with just nine seconds left to give the Eagles a 24-20 win, dropping the Titans to 0-2.

“They executed better in critical moments,” said head coach Robert Saleh after the loss.

After an uneven start in Week 1, quarterback Cam Ward took a step forward against the Eagles, connecting on 12-of-20 passes for 183 yards, good for an Adjusted Yards per Attempt of 9.2, one of the best marks of his career. But this is still a team that looks a long way from contending for a playoff spot, even if some winnable games are coming up including a date with the Giants this week (who may be without Jaxson Dart) and a home game against Cleveland in October.

4. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

After signing a big contract extension this offseason, Baker Mayfield is off to a slow start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He has completed 71% of his passes — which is good — but has posted an Adjusted Net Yards per Attempt of just 5.0.

That ranks him 27th in the league among qualified passers, and below league average.

The bigger concern for Tampa Bay, however, comes on the defensive side of the ball. After giving up 33 points to Joe Burrow and company in a Week 1 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, the Buccaneers gave up 23 points to Deshaun Watson in a loss to the Browns last Sunday.

With games coming up against Brian Flores and the Vikings in Week 3, the Packers in Week 4, and the Cowboys in Week 5, the Buccaneers have a lot of work to do to get back in the mix. Being in the NFC South helps — as they are only one game out of first place even sitting at 0-2 — but if that defense cannot improve in a hurry, this could be a long season in Tampa Bay.

3. Los Angeles Chargers

There are plenty of reasons to put the Los Angeles Chargers lower on this.

One such reason is the little bit of history the Chargers made last Sunday, as they lost a second home game to a team that finished below .200 the prior season. That puts Los Angeles on a list where the only other entry is the Racine Tornadoes from the 1926 season.

Racine folded operations a few weeks later.

Then there is the schedule, which quite frankly puts 0-9 right on the table given how bad the Chargers have looked these past two weeks. Jim Harbaugh and company face the Bills, the Seahawks, the Broncos, the Chiefs, the Rams, the Texans, and the Ravens over the next two months. That … that is tough.

The talent is there (which keeps them high on this particular list, along with what we have seen from the other 0-2 teams) but this woeful start combined with the upcoming schedule makes it hard to believe a turnaround is coming.

2. Indianapolis Colts

It was a tough start to the season for the Indianapolis Colts, who gave up 41 points in a Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

Week 2 was a little better, as the Colts went into Arrowhead Stadium and forced overtime against the Kansas City Chiefs, only to come up short when the offense got conservative at the end of their final possession, settling for a game-tying field goal and giving Patrick Mahomes a chance to get the Chiefs in position for the game-winning field goal.

Moral victories are not counted in the standings, however.

The presence of Jonathan Taylor certainly helps, and Daniel Jones has looked healthy coming back from his Achilles injury. And in the AFC South, 0-2 means you are just one game out of first place, with the Jacksonville Jaguars leading the way at 1-1. But this week is almost a de facto playoff game for the Colts, as they square off against the 0-2 Houston Texans. The loser will slip a game further back in the division, and have a loss to a rival in hand come tiebreaker time.

1. Houston Texans

Resting on the coffee table in our family room is one of the latest editions of Sports Illustrated Kids. It is the magazine’s NFL Preview installment. On the cover, with the headline “Too Hot to Handle,” are five members of the Houston Texans defense.

The subheadline reads “Let ‘Em Cook: The Texans’ Defense is Climbing the Scoville Scale.”

But through two games, that defense has not been as hot as advertised. After giving up 36 points to Josh Allen and the Bills in Week 1, Houston allowed another 20 points in a Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

That makes Houston the 24th-ranked team in the league in scoring defense through two games.

Given the talent on that side of the ball, we will not panic about the defense just yet. The offensive production in Week 2, however, is worrisome. That might be more of a reflection of an improved Cincinnati defense than anything else, but the clock is ticking on C.J. Stroud and company.

A win over Indianapolis rights the ship, and gets Houston right back into the mix in the AFC South. Given the talent on both sides of the ball, that should be the start to a playoff run.

But an 0-3 start would be a much different cover story.

item.title: ‘Things I think’: Jaxson Dart injury, Rams give Giants a reality check
item.description: Monday night showed us that the Giants, while they are better, have a long way to go to become championship-caliber.
item.content:encoded:
The big thing everyone connected with the New York Giants is thinking about in the wake of Monday’s lopsided 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams is the health of quarterback Jaxson Dart. The Giants appear to have dodged the worst possible news, with the expectation that imaging on Tuesday will confirm a sprained MCL.

Monday’s outcome, though, exposed a number of things about the 2026 Giants that we have to talk about, and that they have to be concerned about. Let’s look at some of the ‘things I think’ as the Giants try to move on and get ready for a Week 3 game against the Tennessee Titans.

We have to start with Dart.

Not the worst case, but not good

“We’ll know more when we find out more,” Giants coach John Harbaugh said after the game.

Harbaugh did allow that there was “no question” that seeing Dart moving around on the sideline after the game and believing his injury wasn’t season-ending was comforting.

“The fact that it’s not that outcome that you’re talking about, the devastating outcome, is really good news,” he said.

Dart’s injury had nothing to do with all of the ongoing chatter about him not being willing to protect himself by sliding or getting out of bounds when he runs, something he actually did do in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys.

Dart got hurt in the pocket, which, thanks to the NFL rulebook, is actually the safest place for quarterbacks. There is nothing the rules can do, though, to prevent getting sandwiched between two pass rushers and getting your knee inverted in a manner in which it’s not meant to bend.

Maybe Dart misses two weeks. Maybe he misses six. The Giants, driven hard by Harbaugh this spring and summer, are about to best tested in a way they hoped not to be this season.

Giants players have seen and dealt with injuries before. They were saying the right things after the game. Winstn did admit losing Dart was a “gut punch” in the moment.

“You get ready to play another one,” Winston said of what the Giants do now. “You got another opponent and they don’t care.”

“We’re going to continue to practice hard, get out there, be more intentional about what we’ve got to do, what we’ve got to accomplish. Rally around Jameis,” said Malik Nabers.

“For us to come in here and … get punched in the face, you have to get back up and keep going,” right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said. “There’s still 15 more rounds.”

The bigger issue, beyond how long Dart will be out, is that Monday night exposed many truths about the 2026 Giants. Let’s get to them.

Pump the brakes on expectations

I have been warning for months not to expect a New England Patriots-like turnaround from 4-13 one year to 13-4 and a Super Bowl-berth the next. The most optimistic outcome I could summon for the 2026 Giants when asked to make a prediction was 9-8. Yet, after an impressive season-opening victory over the Dallas Cowboys national analysts were jumping the bandwagon and fans were dreaming big dreams.

The Rams brought those out-sized expectations crashing down to earth.

Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Aaron Donald, Sean McVay and the rest of a supremely talented Rams’ roster showed the Giants and a national football audience what a Super Bowl-contending teams looks like.

It ain’t the Giants.

The floor has been raised with the accomplished John Harbaugh as head coach. The eventual ceiling? Unknown, but the Rams exposed a number of things that have to be dealt with to find out.

What are some of those things?

Running the ball without Dart

The Giants averaged 2.5 yards per rush Monday night. Through two games, they average 3.7 yards per carry, 22nd in the NFL. Take out Dart’s 11 carries for 54 yards in Week 1, that average dips to 3.5 yards. The Giants’ longest non-Dart run in two games is 13 yards.

The Giants are built to be a run-first team, and that has to get better.

After a turnover games the Giants the ball on the Rams’ 11-yard line they ran four times (including a 3-yard loss negated by a Los Angeles penalty), got nowhere, and settled for a deflating field goal when down 14-0.

Do they have the interior blocking or the backs to make that better? Maybe, but they need to be better than they were Monday. The Andrew Thomas injury might complicate matters. The Giants were outclassed up front by the Rams. Plus, they had several plays where the timing and execution were off, with players running into each other.

The pass rush

The simple question is, where is it?

This is an incredible stat:

The Giants have just one sack and five quarterback hits in two games. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson wants to rush just four, which isn’t a horrible goal considering the state of the secondary, but through two games Dak Prescott and Matthew Stafford have stood in the pocket and done basically whatever they wanted to do.

The Giants’ sack percentage of 1.52 is worse than every team in the league except the Miami Dolphins.

With Brian Burns injured, fixing that quickly won’t be easy.

About that secondary

Who knew at the start of training camp that the Giants would miss Tae Banks as much as they did last night? Cornerbacks Colton Hood and Greg Newsome, along with safety Tyler Nubin, were not up to the task of defending Davante Adams. The linebackers and safeties weren’t up to the task of covering tight end Terrance Ferguson.

There are no easy fixes. Dream about a Joey Porter trade if you must, but the Giants really need an offseason where they can add talent via free agency and the draft.

Run defense

One week after an impressive performance vs. Dallas, the Giants allowed the Rams to run for 163 yards on 28 carries, 5.8 per rush. Through two games, the Giants are giving up 5.0 yards per rush, 28th in the NFL.

Talent-wise, this is another area the Giants are going to have to Band-Aid, duct-tape, and scheme around until they can get to the offseason and try to add more young talent.

It was disturbing to see 2025 second-round pick Darius Alexander, who simply does not seem to be improving as a run defender, inactive. The Giants used journeyman Josh Tupou, a practice squad player who appeared in six games with the Ravens the past two seasons, and C.J. Okoye, a Nigerian-born defensive tackle who knew nothing about football until 2023, instead of Alexander.

Not a good sign.

The upcoming schedule

Not that long ago, the upcoming four games (vs. the Tennessee Titans, vs. the Arizona Cardinals, at the Washington Commanders, vs. the New Orleans Saints) was looked at a stretch where the Giants might be able to run off some victories.

Now? Maybe it is still a softer part of the schedule, but there isn’t any certainty that the Giants will be able to take advantage of it.

My last thought is this:

Months of good vibes that began when Harbaugh was hired crumbled on Monday night with the Dart injury and the reality check provided by the Rams. The season, as Eluemunor indicated, will be defined by the next 15 rounds.

Do the Giants have the ability to punch back? We’ll find out.

item.title: Dan Campbell on Kerby Joseph: We're trying to get him back, but he's not ready
item.description: The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.

Head coach Dan Campbell said at a Monday press conference that Branch, who is coming off a torn Achilles, is probably closer to returning from the physically unable to perform list than Joseph. Joseph has been dealing with knee problems since early last season and Campbell was asked on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday what he would say to someone who wonders if Joseph is going to play at all this season.

"I wish I could make you feel good," Campbell said. "I can’t make you feel good. It’s going to come as it comes, and he’s not ready. We’re trying to get him there as fast as we can, and we’re trying to be as smart about it as we can. If he’s ready, when he’s ready, of course we want to play him and get him on the field."

The Lions lost another safety when Avonte Maddox went down in Week 2 and they added veteran Jalen Mills to their practice squad on Monday to help bolster their depth. Barring a major change for Joseph, they may remain on the search for help at the back end of the defense all year.

item.title: Eagles News: Philadelphia should lean on Jalen Hurts and the passing game more
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/22/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Remember the “Let Russ Cook” movement? When Russell Wilson was in his prime as a passer but the Seattle Seahawks insisted on the running the ball over and over, even if it wasn’t working? Feels like we’re reaching that point in Philly. The run game isn’t there for the Eagles right now. Maybe it’ll eventually come together … but maybe not. Hurts is looking great. Lean into that on early downs instead of regularly forcing him to bail the offense out on 3rd-and-long!

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

The Day After – Hurts So Good – Iggles Blitz

It sure feels like that could be happening again. Hurts has a new scheme and a new OC in Sean Mannion. Hurts is driven to show the world, especially his doubters, that he can be a top flight QB in the NFL. He’s thrown 5 TDs so far this year. He didn’t hit that number until Week 4 last season. The Eagles came into the season expecting to rely on their 2024 formula. Combine a top OL with a dominant run game and a stifling defense. That idea hasn’t worked so far. The Eagles coaches need to consider changing their approach. They should lean on Hurts and the passing game more. Attack on early downs instead of running into loaded boxes. I don’t know that Nick Sirianni would be willing to do this, but he really ought to consider it. Hurts is the team’s best player right now. Embrace that and see what he can do in a more aggressive offense. He’s shown in the past that he can thrive in the right situation.

Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3 – ESPN

I think … Jalen Hurts is settling into the Sean Mannion offense. At a team level, I do not love what I’m seeing from the Eagles’ offense. The offensive line looks worse even than it did in 2025, and the running game is suffering as a result — fifth-lowest yards before contact per rush among all teams through two weeks. For the amount of money poured into that unit, that’s scary. Hopefully, guard Landon Dickerson comes back from his injury looking back to form, but we haven’t seen that form in a while; same for center/guard Cam Jurgens. I’m not holding my breath. But Hurts’ Week 2 performance against the Titans was about as good of a game a quarterback can have with a dead-in-the-water rushing attack. Hurts had nine third-down conversions in this game, the most single-game third-down conversions he has had. With no running game, Hurts averaged 7.9 yards to go on third down, well above his career average, and still got big gains in the air, converting three third-and-12 or longer downs (the most in a game in his career). Perhaps most notable of these late conversions was the first one. Hurts hits an intermediate in-breaker to Dontayvion Wicks between the layers of the defense.

Updated: Caleb Williams avoided serious injury; is likely ‘week-to-week’ – Windy City Gridiron

Hard to imagine Williams playing if he doesn’t even practice for the game at all.

UPDATE: Johnson said Williams probably won’t practice this week, but he won’t rule him out for Monday night against the Eagles, adding, “We’re saying week to week with him right now. We’ll see where he’s at as the week progresses and how long that means… It was somewhat encouraging, the report we got.” “He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here,” Johnson said about Williams. “We’ll see what that looks like. Here’s what I know. This guy’s a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I’ll double down on that. He gets back – he has in the past – a lot faster than what people can anticipate and so I’m not putting a timeline on this. We’re going to say week to week. He’s going to attack this with everything that he knows.”

NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 3 edition – PhillyVoice

4) Eagles (2-0): The Eagles have significant issues, most notably that their run game stinks and the offensive line in general is not playing well. Also, the defense has underwhelmed, although that’s not out of the ordinary early in the season under Vic Fangio. BUT… the major box that has been checked so far is the play of Jalen Hurts, which is kind of a big deal.

Zach Ertz arrives in Philly, ‘honored’ to be back in Eagles green – NBCSP

“My mom was in tears. My wife was ecstatic,” Ertz said. “My kids, they don’t really understand but I already had the boys practicing the E-A-G-L-E-S chant. So overall it was good. It’s exciting times and, like I said, just really happy to be back. And honored to be back in the Eagles green. But at the end of the day, I’ve got to go earn whatever role I can. So that’s the goal right now.” Ertz, 35, is signing to the Eagles’ practice squad to start. But his arrival comes as we learned on Monday that starting tight end Dallas Goedert will miss the next few weeks with an MCL sprain. If Ertz can get caught up to speed quickly, he’s going to have a chance to contribute as early as Monday night in Chicago.

Bowen: Maybe the Eagles could just try to be normal, for once? – PHLY Eagles

One consequence of this is that the Eagles are constantly in third-and-long, asking Jalen Hurts to bail them out. So far, he has done that, but an offense that lives in third-and-long is an offense that is ripe for disaster. Comrade EJ Smith’s excellent postgame piece from Nashville noted the SumerSports observation that the Eagles have the largest difference between early-down offensive success rate vs. Late-down success rate to start a season since 2022. It’s 31.5% on first down, 60.6% on third down, a tribute to Hurts and to his receiving corps. (Which now seems likely to be missing Dallas Goedert, at least for a little while). Left tackle Jordan Mailata’s postgame comments were encouraging, pointing out that an O-line needs continuity, and that presumably, the current unit can now get some time on task.

Eagles survive Titans behind Jalen Hurts. Here’s what Philadelphia must fix next – The Athletic

The Eagles averaged 2.5 yards on their stretch run concepts. The tape again showed blockers failing to secure the seam that could break a big run. Cam Jurgens, playing left guard for the first time, whiffed on linebacker Cody Barton, who limited Tank Bigsby to a 4-yard gain on a play that had room to be much more. The Eagles later attempted two stretch plays behind right guard Tyler Steen. The runs totaled three yards. The plodding concepts seemed to lead the Eagles into a first-and-10 toss play in the second quarter in which Will Shipley gained seven yards. Mannion also ran the pistol for the first time — apparently to stimulate the run game. They ran four plays in the set. They brought in a tight end as a fullback on two of the plays. Mundt was in the backfield when Hurts pulled a third-and-4 zone-read keeper and gained the four yards he needed. Bigsby gained 11 yards on three rushes. At times, the Eagles found more success running the ball inside from the shotgun. Bigsby gained four yards on a second-and-10 run on the first drive. Shipley later gained five yards on a similar first-down run. The offensive line also wasn’t always at fault. Running backs seemed to shift away from intended holes in search of the big run. Barkley cut rightward into the backs of blockers on the first play. Bigsby did a similar thing on a later second-and-8 run, cutting rightward into traffic when a narrow hole was available to the left. The Eagles had no rushes of 10 or more yards for only the fifth time since 2021. Such explosive runs are vital to a system that intends to play pass and run off each other by creating similar looks. “Our runs are all three or four yards,” Johnson said. “Hardly any explosives, which was tough for us. When you don’t have the explosives, it’s hard to sell the play action and all that. We had to make it work there in the second half.”

NFL Week 2 Sunday aftermath: Surprising Raiders, soaring Chiefs and sinking Chargers in spotlight – NFL.com

While we’re here, this is how I’d rank the eight 2-0 teams — with the Giants looking to join the list by beating the Rams on Monday night — starting with the most impressive through two weeks: 1) Buffalo Bills, 2) San Francisco 49ers, 3) Seattle Seahawks, 4) Kansas City Chiefs, 5) Minnesota Vikings, 6) Cincinnati Bengals, 7) Las Vegas Raiders, and 8) Philadelphia Eagles.

Spadaro: The wide receivers? They are delivering – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

This was, without question, the biggest conversation point of the entire offseason. Who would step up and be the producer(s) in the wide receiver room for the Philadelphia Eagles? The lineup changed, but how would that impact the offense? Two games into the season isn’t a full-scale sample size, but it’s enough to feel really good about where the Eagles are in that department. DeVonta Smith, coming off a 10-catch, 117-yard, 1-touchdown game, dressed next to Dontayvion Wicks, who caught 5 passes for 74 yards, and who dressed next to Darius Cooper, who caught the game-winning pass in the back of the end zone, as the Eagles worked their way out of Nissan Stadium in Nashville to return to Philadelphia on Sunday night after the thrilling 24-20 win over Tennessee. The wide receivers? They are delivering. “We’re all talented players. Getting a chance to show what you can do, that’s what you want in the NFL,” said Wicks, who has 7 catches for 147 yards and a touchdown in the two Eagles wins. “This offense gives us opportunities to make plays. We go out there and do our jobs. Every player in our room is capable of going out there and doing it. For Coop to make that catch, we’re all happy for him. He works hard and he’s a great player.”

The Eagles Have Thrown Seven Screen Passes This Season for -15 Yards – Crossing Broad

With that caveat, the Eagles have now run seven screen this year for a total of -15 yards. They’ve completed 5 of these 7 passes and the other two were blown up by defensive linemen. They’re averaging -2.1 yards per screen attempt.

Eagles’ silence on their role in the Macklemore mess has become deafening – Inquirer

But honestly, I found it even more disturbing that neither Lurie nor anyone from the Eagles organization feels they owe any explanation at all to the city, let alone thousands of people who drained their bank accounts for a concert that was nothing like it had been advertised. To be sure, there’s no harder dialogue in the world than the conflict in the Middle East, but the Birds committed two penalties against open expression — one of alleged censorship, and one of their own public silence. On Thursday, I texted Bob Lange, the Eagles’ senior vice president for communications, with questions about Lurie’s reported role in collaborating with Kraft and for a clarification on what their policies are around free speech at football games, concerts, and other events that take place at the stadium they operate. “If we have anything to share, we will let you know,” Lange responded.

The play call Brian Daboll probably wants back – Music City Miracles

Instead, Brian Daboll called a bootleg that ended in a sack back at the 18-yard line. JC Latham whiffed on Jalen Carter, who had apparently picked up a tell from Ward when watching tape.

Jaxson Dart injury: NY Giants’ QB suffers left knee injury vs. Rams – Big Blue View

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a left knee injury on the team’s first drive Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams. Initial reports are that the injury is believed to be a sprained MCL. Dart will undergo an MRI on Tuesday. “We’ll know tomorrow,” head coach John harbaugh said after the game. “That’s [MCL sprain] in the neighborhood of it, I would say.” Dart was sandwiched between Rams defenders Byron Young and Josaiah Stewer on a third-and-8 incompletion to Theo Johnson from the Rams’ 41-yard line. Dart did walk slowly off the field under his own power. Dart has been ruled out. GM Joe Schoen told ESPN that the quarterback is “going to be OK.” ESPN’s Jordan Ranaan reported that Dart wanted to return to the game. After the game, Giants running back Cam Skattebo confirmed that Dart wanted to get back into the game. He added that he thinks Dart will be back on the field ‘In the next few weeks’.

Cowboys vs. Commanders Stock Report: Dak Prescott and offense up, defense still shaky – Blogging The Boys

Stock Down: Christian Parker. It is difficult to say that Christian Parker’s stock is “down” relative to last week because it was about as low as it can be. From Game 1 to Game 2 I suppose you could argue he even improved in a vacuum, but we are talking about going from an F to an F+ here. Consider that the Cowboys have played 16 defensive possessions so far this season. The New York Giants managed to infiltrate the Cowboys’ 40-yard line on six of their seven, and the Washington Commanders crossed that territory on seven of their nine. The Cowboys have allowed opposing offenses to get into field goal range on 13 of these 16 possessions! It is early in his career, he is still figuring it out, and all of that jazz, but that is in no way an excuse. The Cowboys clearly have an offense that can lead to the team accomplishing some serious things, but if the defense can’t even hold their own on the other side then it is going to be a disaster similar to last year.

Commanders vs. Cowboys (game one) – Studs and Duds – Hogs Haven

HC Dan Quinn: Talk about being on the Hot Seat! Dan Quinn’s backside might be so hot right now, that if he tried to wipe with extra-soft Charmin, he’d likely go up in flames! But Mark, that’s not very professional of you… You know what — we’re past that point! He’s officially a lame duck!

Lions bring back veteran safety to practice squad – Pride Of Detroit

The Detroit Lions made a minor move on Monday, signing safety Jalen Mills to their practice squad. He takes up the vacant spot on the 16-man squad after the Lions signed Levi Onwuzurike to the 53-man roster over the weekend. Mills’ signing is a direct reaction to the Lions losing starting safety Avonte Maddox for the entire season due to a foot injury that will require surgery. On Monday afternoon, Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that the team was in the market for a veteran safety—and possibly more.

Marvin Harrison Jr. has gone from can’t-miss prospect to Cardinals’ afterthought – SB Nation

Marvin Harrison Jr. was different. He fell on the other end of the spectrum. Everything in the pre-draft process made him look like a home run pick, a player with every single trait needed to succeed in the NFL. There was nothing about how he played at Ohio State or looked at the combine that could ever indicate he would struggle in the NFL — and in picking him it seemed like the Cardinals were destined to find their next Larry Fitzgerald. Three years in and the dream has collapsed. Against the Seahawks on Sunday he didn’t register a single catch, locking his season statistics at a paltry two catches for 44 yards. In addition, he’s being phased out of Mike LaFleur’s offense, as Harrison is being pulled off the field on rushing downs, and getting fewer snaps as Michael Wilson has passed by him as the team’s No. 1 receiver, and now even 31-year-old Kendrick Bourne is being more involved in the offense than Harrison is.

item.title: 49ers have the best odds in the NFC to make the playoffs through 2 weeks
item.description: The Niners are impressing everyone to start the season.
item.content:encoded:
It’s been only two weeks, but the San Francisco 49ers are looking like a true Super Bowl contender this year after a pair of dominant wins to start the season.

After a 27-7 blowout over the Los Angeles Rams as an underdog, the 49ers cruised past the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, scoring touchdowns on each of their first five drives as they won 35-13 in a game where they never really looked in trouble.

It was an amazing day for Brock Purdy, who completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns, while adding a third on the ground. San Francisco didn’t need much on the ground because their passing game was so dominant, as Purdy connected well with George Kittle and Mike Evans, who led the team in receiving.

Heading into the season, the 49ers were seen as a playoff contender, but most still viewed them as the clear No. 3 team in their division behind the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and powerhouse Los Angeles Rams. Well, after two weeks, the 49ers have the best odds in the NFC to reach the playoffs at -320, according to FanDuel.

Behind them are the Seahawks (-300) and Rams (-290), while the Philadelphia Eagles (-270) are the only other team above -200 odds. Now, when it comes to Super Bowl odds, the 49ers are still behind both the Rams (+650) and Seahawks (+950) at +1000 odds, while ranking behind the Buffalo Bills (+750) and alongside the Baltimore Ravens (+1000).

San Francisco has a big three-week stretch coming up. They first face the Arizona Cardinals at home in Week 3, giving them a chance at a 2-0 start in the division, before facing the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks (road). If they can find a way to go 2-1 in that stretch, the 49ers will be in a great position through the first quarter of the season, looking like true Super Bowl contenders.

Of course, as always with this team, the key will be health. The 49ers have dealt with a ton of injury issues ahead of the season, and they had two more receiver injuries on Sunday, as Demarcus Robinson had an ankle issue, while Mike Evans had a hip issue. Evans’s doesn’t seem to be serious, while Robinson will likely miss a couple of weeks.

But the 49ers look much more complete as a team through two weeks than what they showed last season, especially on defense. In addition, Brock Purdy has looked sharp to start the season and is slowly emerging as a dark horse MVP candidate.

Currently, he sits as fourth in MVP odds at +950 behind Josh Allen (+250), Joe Burrow (+850), and Patrick Mahomes (+850). This upcoming three-game stretch will tell us a lot about Purdy, as the 49ers will be in some tougher game environments, but there’s been a lot of good from the San Francisco quarterback to start the year.

When the schedule initially came out during the offseason, the 49ers’ end-of-season schedule looked like a gauntlet. From Weeks 10 to 17, they face the Dallas Cowboys (road), Minnesota Vikings (Mexico City), Seattle Seahawks, New York Giants (road), Los Angeles Rams (home), Los Angeles Chargers (road), Kansas City Chiefs (road), and Philadelphia Eagles.

Outside of the Chargers, each of those teams has looked good to start the year. That makes it imperative to have a strong start. So far, so good.

item.title: NFL Week 3 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including sliding Chargers and surging Vikings
item.description: Oddsmakers have adjusted after some hot and cold starts from teams.
item.content:encoded:
NFL oddsmakers know what they're doing.

Before Monday night's game in Week 2, everything was about as even as could be on sides and totals. Favorites were 16-15 against the spread, while we had 16 unders and 15 overs. The favored Rams and the under hit on Monday night, which prevented everything from being exactly .500 after two weeks. Lower-scoring games in Week 2 led to the under hitting in nine of the first 15 games of the week.

Here are the five top betting storylines for Week 3 of the NFL season:

The Chargers are plummeting

The betting market has finally lost faith in the Chargers. The opening line for Chargers at Bills was Buffalo -3. It moved to -4.5 on the lookahead line last week, via 4for4.com. The Chargers lost their second game in a row as a favorite of a touchdown or more in Week 2, and the line moved up to Bills -7. The Chargers have been the NFL's biggest disappointment while the Bills have been excellent over the first two weeks, so it's not a big surprise that the line moved to a full touchdown. At least any serious survival pool players who are still alive won't think of taking the Chargers this week.

Respect for the Vikings

The Vikings are 2-0 and oddsmakers are taking notice. Or maybe they're taking notice of how bad the Buccaneers looked in falling to 0-2 with a home loss to the Browns. The Vikings are 1.5-point road favorites against the Buccaneers. Minnesota is expected to get quarterback Kyler Murray back in the lineup after he cleared concussion protocol. Minnesota hasn't needed him, as it has gone 2-0 with Carson Wentz at quarterback. After a win as a 4.5-point underdog at Chicago last week, the Vikings are being viewed as a playoff contender. They're favored to win the NFC North at DraftKings, while other sites like BetMGM and FanDuel have the Vikings just behind the Lions in the division odds.

Cowboys are underdogs in Brazil

A good performance by the Cowboys in Week 2 and a late-game collapse by the Ravens didn't affect the perception of either team too much. The Ravens are 3-point favorites against the Cowboys for their game in Brazil this week. Baltimore is coming off a last-minute loss at home to the Saints, but oddsmakers have been high on the Ravens going back to the offseason and aren't backing down. The Cowboys beat the Commanders 37-20 with Dak Prescott throwing four touchdowns. One thing to keep an eye on: There are questions about the turf at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro after rainfall over the past six weeks, but the NFL has said it is not concerned. The total for the game is 52.5.

Bears, Commanders have QB questions

The Bears saw Caleb Williams go down with what ended up being a hamstring injury, and the Commanders lost Jayden Daniels to a dislocated left elbow. Williams' injury isn't considered too serious but his status for Week 3 is unknown. Daniels is seeing specialists and could miss time. To start the week, the Commanders are 6.5- or 7-point underdogs at home to the Seahawks. The Bears are 3.5-point underdogs against the Eagles.

According to the survey of oddsmakers by Yahoo Sports' Ben Fawkes, the difference between Williams and his backup Tyson Bagent is about 4.1 points on the spread. The difference between Daniels and his backup Marcus Mariota is a little less than five points on the spread. Each line could move once there are definitive status updates on each quarterback for Week 3.

Rams bounce back

The Rams have dealt with plenty of adversity already this season. They lost the opener, then Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua were out for Week 2. Still, seeing them completely dominate the Giants in Week 2 reinforced their status as Super Bowl favorite. For Week 3, the Rams are 2.5-point favorites for a tough road game at the Denver Broncos. The Broncos have historically been strong in September, in large part because of the altitude factor early in the season. And despite that and some key injury issues, the Rams are nearly a field-goal favorite at Denver. They are also maintaining their position as the favorite to win the Super Bowl at +600.

item.title: Packers Film Room: Dashing for a dagger
item.description: Looking at the final offensive play of the game & why it worked the way it did.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, we talked about the Green Bay Packers’ use of Dash motion and how they used the Vikings defensive tendencies to hit a play behind it. Today, we’re looking at that same motion and a play the Packers hit off of it in Week 2 against the New York Jets.

Before we get started, let’s talk about the type of motion. “Dash” motion is something we’ve been seeing quite a bit of around the league this year. It’s a type of slow motion that arcs behind the line, then run towards the line at the snap for a block.

Over the first two weeks of this season, the Packers have used this motion 10 times. They have run on 8 of those for an average gain of 6.5 yards, and they have run the same power concept on every one of those runs. The Dash motion man kicks out the EMOL (End Man on Line), the right guard pulls and works as a lead, the rest of the line blocks down. (I have the pullers in blue to make it easier to see.)

Last week, the Packers hit a backside slant late, as the Vikings were blitzing the backside every time the Packers showed that motion. This week, they had the backside WR run a Bubble.

That Bubble tag was on the backside of every one of these plays this week. Last week the only time we saw a route run on the backside of one of these plays was the slant to Matthew Golden that we covered last week.

The Jets played this route a couple different ways. When they aligned a man tight to Golden, that defender aligned outside and shadowed the bubble. (Bottom of the screen on the next clip.)

When the Jets were in off coverage, the safety over Golden would shadow the bubble motion. (Top of the screen on the next clip.)

Now, to the last play.

After stopping the Jets on their first possession of overtime, the Packers drove down the field. With 5:47 remaining in overtime, they were facing 1st & 10 at the Jets’ 22 yard line. With the Jets already having had a possession, a field goal would win it, but you want to drive a little closer. Trey Smack had been a perfect 3/3 on field goals and extra points up until that point (due in some part to a great snap-and-hold operation), but you want to make this a little easier on him.

The Packers come out in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR) in a completely balanced set: one wide receiver split to each side, an in-line tight end to each side, and a single back behind the QB. Matthew Golden [0] is split wide to the left and Christian Watson [9] is wide to the right. The cornerback over Golden is shaded to the inside shoulder and the safety is playing on the hash. This is important.

Before the snap, Mark Redman [86] starts his Dash motion, triggering the play. At the snap, Golden bubbles out. Instead of handing it off – or throwing to Golden on the Bubble – Love throws a lollipop up the field. The cornerback is blitzing off the edge to try to stop the run from the backside, so he’s in no position to make a play on this ball. The safety playing so far inside is also in no position to make a play on this. By throwing it over the top, Love avoids any opportunity for the defender to that side to make a play.

A couple interesting things here. The Jets did not really blitz their cornerbacks in this game. They blitzed on 31.25% of their defensive snaps (per SumerSports), but, unless I missed some, this was the only time they blitzed a cornerback in this game.

More than anything, I think the alignment of the cornerback and safety is what informed the decision to throw this. If the cornerback was playing on Golden’s outside shoulder, I think Love hands the ball off. If the Jets are in off coverage and the safety is over the top, I think Love throws this to Golden on the bubble.

With the cornerback playing the inside shoulder and the safety playing on the hash, Love makes the decision to throw to Golden, but throw further outside and up-field than simply throwing the Bubble (since the cornerback could have a chance to knock down a throw to the flat). And, since Golden is running a Bubble, Love puts enough air under this ball to allow Golden to adjust as the ball is in the air. The cornerback blitzing makes this more open than it would have been, but even if that cornerback simply played how he had been playing this – a soft mirror on the Bubble – he still would not have been in a great position to defend this.

I love the call in this moment (it was the best run concept on the day for the Packers), but I love seeing the recognition from Love at the line and the adjustment from Golden to be able to make this catch and pick up yards afterwards.

By the time the dust had settled, it was a 14 yard gain, setting up a 26 yard field goal, which Smack knocked through.

item.title: Titans QB Cam Ward showed real progress in Week 2
item.description: Tennessee Titans QB Cam Ward was way better in Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans endured a tough loss in Week 2, losing 24-20 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward showed real growth. Ward was way better than he was in Week 1 versus the Jets, and that progress is good news for the Titans.

Ward finished 13-of-20 for 183 yards. The second-year No. 1 overall selection was better than the box score indicates. Ward was very accurate and decisive.

Ward also rushed for two touchdowns. His playmaking ability on 3rd-and-goal set the offense up for 4th-and-goal from the half-yard line. A QB sneak got Ward into the end zone.

Ward completed 65% of his passing attempts. He only bested that mark in four individual games last season. Ward also averaged an explosive 9.2 yards per pass. That would have been a single-game high during his 2025 rookie campaign.

Ward’s only “miss” was a throw into the end zone for Ayomanor. Poor footwork led to an inaccurate ball behind Ayomanor. It was still catchable, but it should have been a straightforward completion. Ward’s footwork is still in work-in-progress mode. The former Miami standout made up for it with the aforementioned third-down scramble that led to his first rushing score on fourth down.

Ward’s average depth of target (7.1) was also significantly better than his Week 1 aDOT (5.3). Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll did a good job removing some of the concepts Ward struggled with in Week 1. He played with confidence, throwing the ball with anticipation while finding the explosive plays that lacked versus the Jets.

The Titans’ 2026 season is all about Ward’s progress. Week 1 was a discouraging showing, but Ward already looked significantly more comfortable in Daboll’s offense against a stout Eagles defense. Hopefully he continues taking positive steps forward versus the New York Giants in Week 3.

item.title: Colts reunite veteran WR with Daniel Jones after Alec Pierce injury
item.description: The Colts are adding a veteran wide receiver to their roster after Alec Pierce aggravated a heel injury in Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts are adding a veteran wide receiver to their roster after Alec Pierce was injured in their Week 2 game against the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Colts have agreed to sign New York Giants receiver Darius Slayton, per multiple reports. Terms of the deal between the two parties were not immediately disclosed.

Slayton, 29, spent the first seven years of his career with the Giants after being a fourth-round pick out of Auburn. He appeared in 106 games for the franchise with 78 starts and racked up 296 catches, 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns across his seven seasons.

Slayton figures to be asked to help replace Pierce as the Colts' primary speed threat. The 29-year-old has averaged an impressive 15 yards per reception across his career, though he had just a 72.9 passer rating when targeted on throws of 20-plus yards during the 2026 season in Indianapolis.

It's worth noting that Slayton has built-in chemistry with Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. The Giants selected both in the 2019 NFL Draft and they played together across parts of six seasons in New York.

Here's more to know about Slayton's fit with the Colts and how his role could be impacted by Pierce's injury.

Alec Pierce injury update

Pierce aggravated an injury in his surgically repair left heel during the Colts' "Sunday Night Football" game against the Chiefs in Week 2. The veteran receiver was running a route when he pulled up in pain and hopped to the sideline.

Pierce did not return to the game and was spotted wearing a boot and using crutches after the game.

Colts coach Shane Steichen did not immediately provide an update on Pierce's injury or timeline to return, but NFL Media's Ian Rapoport reports Pierce is expected "to be out several weeks" because of the ailment.

Pierce is choosing to attempt to rehabilitate the injury without surgery.

Colts WR depth chart

Pierce's absence, along with the addition of Slayton, will create a new pecking order within Indianapolis' receiver room. Below is a projection of how the Colts' receiver rotation could look in Week 3 and beyond:

  1. Josh Downs
  2. Keenan Allen
  3. Laquon Treadwell
  4. Darius Slayton
  5. Ashton Dulin
  6. Deion Burks

Downs will be the Colts' clear-cut No. 1 receiver after getting a team-high nine targets against the Chiefs. Following him will be the veteran duo of Allen and Treadwell, who rank second and third among receivers on the team in offensive snaps played.

Slayton will have a chance to push Allen and Treadwell for playing time, so he could eventually work his way up to the team's No. 2 or No. 3 role. It's also worth noting Allen is reportedly facing an eventual NFL suspension of at least three games, so Slayton will provide insurance in case that happens in 2026.

Meanwhile, Dulin is dealing with an ankle injury that caused him to miss Week 2. He will continue to be a special teams ace, who has a small role on offense, upon his return. Burks, a seventh-round rookie, has only played three offensive snaps during his career to date.

The Colts also have veterans Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Anthony Gould on their practice squad. Gould, a 2024 fifth-round pick, was called up to help as a kick returner in Week 2 with Dulin out of action.
